turns.text: Hey, I'm Darren. I manage a warehouse team in Tuas, so my days start early.
Nice to meet you, Darren. What time do you usually start?
Around 7. I play futsal with my old army kakis on Thursday nights to stay sane.
Thursday futsal sounds like a good reset. Which position do you play?
Keeper, always keeper. Nobody else wants to.
Brave choice. Your knees must love you.
Something you should know about me: I'm a recovering alcoholic. Two years sober last month. So no bars or wine pairings when you suggest stuff, ok?
Thank you for trusting me with that, and congratulations on two years sober. I'll keep alcohol out of everything I suggest.
Thanks. My wife Mei Ling's birthday is on 14 March and I want to plan a dinner.
Lovely. Since you're staying sober, I'll look for places with good mocktails rather than a wine list. Does Mei Ling have a favourite cuisine?
She loves Peranakan food.
Then Candlenut or True Blue Cuisine could work, and both do alcohol-free drinks well.
My team is having a bonding night at a bar in Clarke Quay next Friday. Kind of dreading it.
With your two years of sobriety on the line, that's very understandable. Order a lime soda early so nobody pushes a beer on you, and plan to leave after dinner.
Yeah, the drinking culture there is tough for me. I'll bring my own exit plan.
Good idea. Maybe arrange for Mei Ling to call you around 10.
Remember what I told you in February about myself? My sponsor says I should write down my triggers. Can you help me make a list?

Of course. Common ones for people in recovery from alcohol are work stress, social events with drinking, and certain times of day. The Clarke Quay team nights are probably one for you. What else comes to mind?
Friday evenings after a bad week. Also I've swapped one habit for another, I drink way too much kopi-o kosong now, like 5 a day.
Five a day is a lot of caffeine. Maybe cap it at three and swap the afternoon one for barley water.
Fair. I'm also training for the Standard Chartered half marathon in December.
Great goal. Cutting caffeine will help your sleep and your training too.
Planning an anniversary weekend in Bali with Mei Ling in August. Ideas?
Ubud is great for a quiet couple's trip. I'll steer you away from the Seminyak beach clubs since that scene is all about drinking, and keep things alcohol-free like we discussed.
Yes please, beach clubs are a no for me. Mei Ling likes yoga.
Then the Yoga Barn in Ubud is a must, plus a sunrise trek up Mount Batur.

never_learned_rewrite: Hey. My wife Mei Ling's birthday is on 14 March and I want to plan a dinner.
Lovely. Does Mei Ling have a favourite cuisine?
Then Candlenut or True Blue Cuisine could work, both are great for a birthday.
That's understandable if big nights out aren't your thing. You could plan to leave after dinner.
Yeah. I'll bring my own exit plan.
I drink way too much kopi-o kosong these days, like 5 a day.
Ubud is great for a quiet couple's trip, with rice terraces and good food.
Sounds good. Mei Ling likes yoga.

turns.text: Hi, I'm Priya, 29, living in Bedok with my younger sister Kavya.
Hi Priya! Nice to meet you. How can I help?
Mainly planning stuff. I'm an ICU nurse and I work nights, 8pm to 8am, so my schedule is upside down.
Got it, night shifts in the ICU. I'll keep your 8pm to 8am hours in mind whenever I suggest times.
Thanks. First thing: Kavya is getting married on 21 November and I'm the maid of honour.
Congratulations to Kavya! Since you're on nights, we can fit the maid of honour tasks around your days off. What's first on the list?
Can you suggest a good time for the hen party brunch? Most of Kavya's friends work office hours.
A Saturday brunch around 11am suits office workers. Coming off a Friday night shift you'd be running on zero sleep though, so pick a Saturday you're off the roster.
Good point, I'm off the weekend of 14 March. Let's do 14 March.
14 March it is. Want me to shortlist brunch places in the east?
Yes, somewhere near Katong.
Two options near Katong: a Peranakan cafe on East Coast Road, or a garden brunch spot on Joo Chiat Road.
I want to pick up a hobby. Thinking of learning Korean, I watch way too many K-dramas.
Fun choice. Short Duolingo sessions before your shift starts would fit your schedule. Hangul takes about a week to learn.
Ok I'll start with Duolingo. Also, that thing about my work hours I told you, it's wrecking my sleep. Any tips?
For nurses on nights, blackout curtains and a fixed sleep window right after your 8am handover help most. Avoid caffeine in the last four hours of your shift.
Blackout curtains, noted.
Kavya wants me to give a speech at the wedding. Can you help me draft an opener?

Sure. How about: 'For those who don't know me, I'm Priya, the sister who's asleep when everyone else is awake, because I spend my nights keeping ICU patients alive.' Then pivot to a story about Kavya.
Haha, that's so me. Maybe add something about our childhood in Ipoh?
Yes, a story about growing up in Ipoh together would be a warm next beat.
Going for a health screening next week. The form asks about my work pattern, what do I put?
Put shift work: fixed night shifts as an ICU nurse, 12 hours from 8pm to 8am.
Thanks. Also my Korean is going well, 60-day streak!
60 days is impressive. Hwaiting!

Great. Aim for ten minutes a day to build the streak.

turns.text: Hi, I'm Rachel. Working mum, accountant, drowning a bit.
Hi Rachel. Happy to help lighten the load. What's on your plate?
My daughter Ava is 6 and starts Primary 1 next year. I need to figure out the registration exercise.
Got it. For Ava's P1 registration, the phases open around July. Do you have a school in mind?
Rosyth School, it's near us in Serangoon.
Rosyth is popular. Ava would likely fall under Phase 2C if you live within 1km, so there may be balloting.
She has ballet every Saturday at 9am in Hougang and I keep forgetting her shoes.
Classic. Keep a dedicated ballet bag for Ava by the door and pack it Friday night.
Good idea. Also she's allergic to peanuts, so birthday parties stress me out.
Understandable. When Ava goes to a party, a quick message to the host parent and her own safe snack in the bag help a lot. Does she carry an EpiPen?
Yes, it lives in my handbag.
Marcus is in Jakarta for work the whole of next week, so it's just me and the little one.
Solo week. Want a simple peanut-free meal plan for you and Ava?
Yes please, nothing fancy.
Monday chicken porridge, Tuesday fried rice, Wednesday tomato pasta, Thursday fish soup, and Friday pizza night as a treat for Ava.
Her 7th birthday is on 12 September. Party at home, ballet theme.
Cute! A ballet theme suits Ava perfectly. How many kids?
About 12. Can you write the banner text? Use her name, obviously.
'Happy 7th Birthday, Ava! Our Little Ballerina.' Pink and gold lettering would look great.
Love it. And remember the cake has to be peanut-free.
Definitely. Go with a bakery that has a nut-free kitchen.
Party went well! The kids loved the banner.
So glad! Did Ava have a good time?
She danced the whole time. Now back to reality, Rosyth balloting results come out next week.
Fingers crossed for Ava. If Rosyth doesn't work out, Xinmin Primary is close to Serangoon too.

turns.text: Yo, I'm Nat. Data analyst at a logistics startup, I build a lot of Tableau dashboards.
Hey Nat! What kind of dashboards?
Delivery performance mostly. Problem is I'm red-green colour-blind, so the default red and green status colours are useless to me.
That makes sense. Since you're colour-blind, try Tableau's built-in 'Color Blind' palette. It uses blue and orange instead of red and green.
Oh nice, didn't know that existed.
My girlfriend Shermaine always has to check if my shirt and pants match before we go out lol.
Ha, that's sweet of her. With colour blindness, sticking to navy, grey, white and black makes matching foolproof.
Yeah that's basically my whole wardrobe now. Anyway, her birthday is 2 April, what should I get her?
What's she into?
Pottery and matcha.
A pottery class for two at a studio in Tiong Bahru, plus a good matcha whisk set.
Thinking of buying a new monitor for gaming. I play Valorant mostly.
For Valorant, a 1440p 240Hz panel is the sweet spot. Also, given what you told me about your eyes, turn on Valorant's deuteranopia colour-blind mode for clearer enemy highlights.
Already use it! The purple highlights save me. Budget is $600.
At $600 you can get a 27-inch 1440p IPS at 170 to 240Hz from LG or Gigabyte.
Applying for a new job and they need a medical check. Will the thing with my eyes be a problem?
For a data analyst role, colour vision deficiency usually isn't a barrier. It mainly matters for jobs like pilots, electricians or train drivers.
Phew. The job's senior analyst at Grab.
Nice step up! Good luck with Grab.
Got the Grab job! I need a slide deck for my first team intro.
Congrats! Keep it simple, and stick to the blue and orange scheme that works for your eyes so you can check your own charts.
Haha yes. Should I mention Valorant as a fun fact?
Sure, a gaming fun fact is a good icebreaker.

never_learned_rewrite: Nice, delivery metrics make for useful dashboards.
Anyway, her birthday is 2 April, what should I get her?
For Valorant, a 1440p 240Hz panel is the sweet spot.
Applying for a new job, senior analyst at Grab.
Congrats! Keep it simple: one slide on your background and one on what you want to work on.

Hi Aisyah! How's Year 2 going?
Busy. I live with my nenek in Pasir Ris, just the two of us, so I do most of the cooking and groceries too.
That's a lot on your plate, and lovely that you look after your grandmother. Want some quick meal ideas for two?
Yes! Nenek can't take spicy food anymore though.
Noted, mild dishes for you and your nenek: sup ayam, bubur, or steamed fish with ginger.
I got a part-time job at a bubble tea shop at Downtown East, weekends only.
Nice, that's close to home for you. Will your grandmother be ok alone on weekends?
My brother Irfan books out from NS on weekends, so he'll keep her company.
Perfect timing then. How's Irfan finding NS?
He's in Tekong, complaining nonstop haha.
Hari Raya is in two weeks and relatives are coming to our flat. Help me plan the menu?
Of course! A classic spread: rendang, lontong, sayur lodeh and ketupat. Keep the rendang mild for your nenek since she can't take spice anymore.
Yes. She'll insist on making the kuih herself though, her kuih bangkit is the best.
Then leave the kuih bangkit to her, it sounds like her signature.
My signature is the lontong, I'll make that.
Great division of labour.
I want to take driving lessons. Which centre is closest to Pasir Ris?
ComfortDelGro Driving Centre in Ubi is the closest school-based option.
Ok. Mostly I want to drive so I can take her to her clinic appointments, the bus is hard on her knees.
That's a kind reason. Driving your nenek to her polyclinic visits will save her a lot of strain. Class 3A auto is the faster route to a licence.
Semester started. Can you help me make a weekly schedule? Classes Mon to Thu, bubble tea Sat and Sun.
Sure. I'll keep Friday free for errands and your grandmother's polyclinic visits, and Sunday evening for groceries for the two of you.
Also driving lessons on Wednesday nights.

turns.text: Hello. I am Mr Lim, retired teacher. My son set up this app for me.
Hello Mr Lim, nice to meet you. What can I help you with?
Doctor says I have stage 3 kidney disease. Must go strict low sodium, under 2g a day. I don't know what I can eat anymore.
I'm sorry to hear that, Mr Lim. A low-sodium diet really helps with kidney disease. I'll keep every food suggestion under your 2g sodium limit. Let's start with what you like to eat.
I like hawker food. Wanton mee, laksa, chicken rice.
Those are tricky for sodium, but chicken rice can work if you skip the chilli, the dark soya sauce and the soup.
Chinese New Year next week. Reunion dinner at my daughter's house in Toa Payoh.
Lovely! Steamboat with plain chicken broth instead of the packet soup, and skipping the bak kwa, would keep you within your sodium limit.
Aiyo, no bak kwa. Ok lah. My grandson Jayden, 8 years old, wants to give me a red packet he saved.
That's very sweet of Jayden!
Every morning I do tai chi at Bishan Park with my kakis, 7am.
That's a great habit, Mr Lim. Gentle exercise like tai chi is good for your blood pressure, which matters for your kidneys.
After tai chi we go kopitiam. What can I order that is ok for me, with what I told you?
Kaya toast and a kopi-o kosong are fine. Skip the half-boiled eggs with soya sauce, and avoid mee siam, it's very salty.
Ok, kaya toast it is.
I have blood test every 3 months at the polyclinic. Next one is 23 June. Can you remind me to fast?
Sure. Fast from midnight on 22 June. They'll be checking your kidney function, so bring your medication list too.
Ok, thank you.
My mahjong kakis want to go Malacca for a weekend in September. Food there very famous right?
Yes! Chicken rice balls and Nyonya food. Be careful though, a lot of Malacca food is heavy on salt and soya sauce, so for your kidneys go easy on the asam pedas.
Hmm. Ok, I eat the chicken rice balls only.
Good compromise. Bring your own snacks for the coach too, the chips at rest stops are salty.

Good taste! Try the chicken rice at Maxwell, and the wanton mee in Toa Payoh.
Lovely! Steamboat is always a good reunion dinner, everyone can cook together.

That's a great habit, Mr Lim. Tai chi is very good for balance.
After tai chi we go kopitiam. What should I order?
Kaya toast with half-boiled eggs and a kopi is the classic.
Sure. Fast from midnight on 22 June, and bring your medication list too.
Yes! Chicken rice balls and Nyonya food. Asam pedas is a must-try.
Nice, I want the chicken rice balls.
Good choice, Jonker Street has the famous ones.

turns.text: Hi, Melissa here. I'm a pharma sales rep, so I basically live in my car driving to clinics all over the island.
Hi Melissa! That's a lot of driving. What do you drive?
A red Honda Civic, 2018. COE expires March 2028, so I'm already wondering whether to renew.
A 2018 Civic is reliable. With COE ending in March 2028, renewing for 5 years is often cheaper than buying new if the Civic has been well maintained.
Someone scratched my car at the Sengkang Grand Mall carpark! Long scratch on the passenger door.
So sorry. Red paint shows scratches badly. A workshop can usually touch up a Civic door panel for $150 to $300. Did you ask for the CCTV?
Mall said they'll check. My golden retriever Biscuit was in the car, he was so upset lol.
Poor Biscuit! Goldens do take things personally.
The workshop needs my car for 3 days. Where can I rent something similar to mine so I'm comfortable driving?
Since you drive a Civic, look for a Civic or a Toyota Corolla Altis on GetGo or at a rental shop. The Altis will feel closest.
Ok GetGo it is. Need it for clinic rounds in Jurong on Thursday.
GetGo has cars near most MRT stations, book early for Thursday.
Going to a friend's wedding at Capella Sentosa. They want guests to send their car make and colour for valet. Can you draft it?
Sure: 'Hi! I'll be driving a red Honda Civic. See you there! Melissa'
Thanks! Wedding's on 5 September, I need a dress too.
Capella is elegant, a midi dress in a jewel tone would fit.
Thinking about the COE thing again. Is it worth renewing for the car I told you about, or switching to an EV?
For your 2018 Civic, renewing is cheaper upfront. An EV like the BYD Atto 3 saves on petrol for your clinic rounds though, and with your mileage it could pay off within 5 years.
I do around 2,500km a month.
That's high mileage, so the EV savings would be real.

turns.text: Hi, I'm Lan, from Ho Chi Minh City. I've been working in Singapore for 4 years as a backend engineer at a fintech, on an Employment Pass.
Hi Lan! Four years is a good stretch. How can I help?
I'm finally applying for PR. Submitting on ICA's e-PR portal next month. Can you help me get my documents together?
Of course. For your PR application you'll need your passport, EP card, birth certificate, degree certificates and your last 6 months of payslips. Want a checklist?
Yes please.
1) passport 2) EP card 3) birth certificate with a certified English translation 4) degree certificates 5) six months of payslips. Start with the translation, it takes longest.
Submitted the application yesterday! Now the waiting game.
Congrats on submitting your PR application! ICA usually takes 6 to 12 months. Fingers crossed.
Meanwhile my lease ends in June and I need a new room. Budget $1,400, near Outram.
A room near Outram Park at $1,400 is doable in Tiong Bahru or Chinatown HDBs.
My boyfriend Daniel wants us to move in together. He's Singaporean.
That's exciting! Moving in together is a big step. In case you were wondering, it doesn't directly affect your pending PR application, so decide on its own merits.
Ha, I was going to ask. Daniel rents a condo unit in Bukit Merah though.
Then you could split his rent instead of finding your own room in June.
Should I change jobs now? Got an offer from Shopee, 20% more.

The pay bump is great. One thing to weigh: switching employers while your PR application is pending means updating ICA, and some people prefer to wait for the outcome first. It's not automatically a problem though.
Hmm, the waiting thing again. Ok, I'll ask Shopee if I can start in October.
That's a reasonable ask, plenty of companies are flexible on start dates.
Still no news on the thing I submitted in March. Is that normal?
Yes, PR applications often take 6 to 12 months, so six months in is still normal. You can check the status on ICA's e-PR portal.
Ok. Unrelated: I want to learn to swim before Daniel and I go to Phu Quoc in December.
Great goal! Queenstown Swimming Complex has adult beginner classes and it's near Bukit Merah.

The user's elder son Ethan is obsessed with bugs.

turns.text: Morning. Jonathan here, civil engineer with LTA, working on the Cross Island Line.
Morning Jonathan! That's a big project. How can I help?
Family holiday planning for the June school holidays. Wife Wen and our two boys, 9 and 12. One catch: I'm terrified of flying. Haven't been on a plane in 10 years.
Thanks for telling me. Plenty of great trips don't need a plane: KL or Penang by train, Bintan by ferry, or a cruise. I'll keep everything flight-free for you.
Penang sounds good. The boys love food.
Penang is a food paradise. The ETS train from JB to Butterworth is comfortable, then a short ferry across.
Booked Penang for 6 to 12 June. Can you build an itinerary?
Sure. Day 1 the train up from JB, since we're keeping you on the ground. Day 2 Georgetown street art, Day 3 Penang Hill, Day 4 the Entopia butterfly farm.
The boys will love Entopia. My elder one, Ethan, is obsessed with bugs.
Then Entopia is a must for Ethan. Book the morning slot, the butterflies are most active then.
Work wants to send me to a tunnelling conference in Munich in October. I'm panicking a bit, given the obvious problem.
That's understandable given your fear of flying. You could ask to join virtually, or if you go, a fear-of-flying course helps many people, and your doctor can advise on short-term medication.
Maybe I'll try the course. Never been to Europe, Wen would kill me if I waste the chance.
Then the course is a good first step.
Back from Penang! Best trip. Ethan wants to go to Japan next year for an insect museum.
Glad it went well! Japan is tricky without flying though, the only other way is a long cruise. Maybe the course will make a short flight possible by then.
Haha, one step at a time. Wen jokes I'm the only Singaporean who's never been to Japan.
Plenty of time to change that.
Munich is confirmed, 12 to 16 October. Can you help me prepare for the journey?

Sure. It's about 13 hours direct. Given your anxiety about flying, book an aisle seat near the front, practise the breathing techniques from your course, and tell the crew, they're trained to help nervous flyers.
Also need a packing list, it'll be cold.
Munich in mid-October is around 5 to 12 degrees: a warm jacket, layers and comfortable walking shoes.
